title: Stochastic scale-trigger analysis and outcomes (Dec 2024)
content:
Executive summary:
We ran a set of controlled experiments across three regions (us-west1, eu-central1, ap-southeast1) to evaluate a probabilistic (stochastic) approach to scale triggers versus the current deterministic min/max-trigger policies. Goal: reduce unnecessary scale events during brief bursts while preserving latency SLOs and lowering unit-cost.

Background / motivation:
- Recent spikes in short-lived bursty request patterns (1–30s) have led to frequent scale-ups and rapid downscales, increasing preemption and rebalancing churn.
- Deterministic thresholds (single-window average) are brittle to noise; we experimented with trigger logic that aggregates short samples and uses a probabilistic decision function to avoid acting on transients.

Experiment goals and acceptance criteria:
- Reduce scale events per hour by >=20% without increasing p95 latency by more than 10%.
- Avoid any sustained p50 degradation; keep cost per token within 5% of baseline.

Key knobs tested (summary):
- Trigger type: deterministic-window vs probabilistic-majority vs weighted-sigmoid-prob
- Up-thresholds tested: 80%, 85%, 90%
- Down-thresholds tested: 45%, 55%, 65%
- Up-window durations: 15s, 30s, 60s
- Down-decay: fixed cooldown, exponential decay (decay factor 0.6 over 5m), and forced-minimum (min hold 3m)
- Min/Max GPU per AZ and regional split (fractional buffer allocation)

Methodology:
- Load profile: replay of production traffic traces from Oct–Nov 2024 with synthetic injected microbursts (peak length distributed 1–30s, amplitude up to 3x baseline)
- Cluster replica: mock GPU instances sized to match n1-standard + A100 perf slices (tokens/sec approximations used for util calculations)
- Metrics recorded: scale-ups/hour, scale-downs/hour, p50/p95/p99 latency, avg GPU utilization, cost delta vs baseline, failed requests, cold-starts per scale event
- Each configuration run for 6h region-sim time and repeated 3x for stability

Experiment matrix (subset):
ID | Trigger | Up-th | Down-th | Up-window | Down-policy | Min GPUs | Max GPUs
E-01 | deterministic | 85% | 50% | 30s | cooldown 2m | 2 | 40
E-02 | prob-majority (3/5 samples) | 85% | 50% | samples 5x6s | cooldown 2m | 2 | 40
E-03 | prob-sigmoid (w=0.4) | 85% | 50% | sliding 30s | exp-decay (0.6, 5m) | 2 | 40
E-04 | prob-sigmoid regional-adjust | 80% (eu) 85% (us) 90% (ap) | 55% | 30s | exp-decay + min-hold 3m | 3 | 50
E-05 | deterministic aggressive | 90% | 45% | 15s | cooldown 1m | 2 | 60

Representative results (aggregated across runs):
- Baseline (E-01 deterministic): scale-ups: 18.7/hr, scale-downs: 20.2/hr, p95 latency: 210ms, avg GPU util: 72%, cost baseline: 0% (reference)
- Prob-majority (E-02): scale-ups: 13.9/hr (-26%), scale-downs: 14.5/hr (-28%), p95 latency: 218ms (+3.8%), avg util: 74%, cost delta: -4.1%
- Prob-sigmoid (E-03): scale-ups: 11.4/hr (-39%), scale-downs: 12.1/hr (-40%), p95 latency: 229ms (+9.0%), avg util: 76%, cost delta: -7.6%
- Prob-sigmoid regional-adjust (E-04): scale-ups: 12.0/hr (-36%), scale-downs: 12.6/hr (-38%), p95 latency: 216ms (+2.9%), avg util: 75%, cost delta: -6.8%
- Deterministic aggressive (E-05): scale-ups: 21.3/hr (+14%), scale-downs: 22.9/hr (+13%), p95 latency: 198ms (-5.7%), cost delta: +5.2%

Observations and interpretation:
- Probabilistic majority voting (E-02) gave a strong reduction in churn with modest p95 impact and good cost improvement.
- Sigmoid-weighted probability (E-03) produced the largest drop in scaling events and best cost reduction but breached the 10% p95 threshold in some runs (edge case bursts where sigmoid delayed upscale).
- Regionally-tuned probabilistic triggers (E-04) can recover p95 while retaining most cost benefits by setting slightly tighter up-thresholds in burstier regions (ap-southeast1) and higher min GPUs for stability.
- Aggressive deterministic thresholds reduce p95 but increase churn and cost, which is undesirable for overall reliability and long-term unit economics.
- Exponential decay for downscale (rather than immediate cooldown) prevents repeated micro down/up cycles and keeps cold-starts lower.

Failure modes / gotchas observed:
- Long-tailed bursts that persist >120s still require immediate deterministic action; probabilistic logic should be combined with an override that triggers if windowed median util exceeds 92% for 30s.
- Rare alignment of multi-region bursts can create global headroom pressure; regional min-GPU constraints and cross-region fallbacks are necessary.
- Telemetry lag (metric scrape delay ~6–8s) increases effective decision latency; we added a compensating sample offset in the probabilistic sampler to reduce false negatives.

Recommendation (ops + rollout):
1) Adopt prob-majority (3-of-5) sampling as default for us-west1 and eu-central1.
2) Implement prob-sigmoid as opt-in for customers targeting max cost efficiency; include a safety override that falls back to deterministic upscaling on sustained high-util (>92% for 30s).
3) Use exponential downscale decay (factor 0.6, 5m window) across all regions to reduce oscillation.
4) Increase regional min GPU to 3 in ap-southeast1 for the next quarter to improve tail latency during frequent microbursts.
5) Add a synthetic burst-simulation job to the nightly test harness; run probabilistic policy against production traces weekly and alert on p95 regressions >8%.

Action items / next steps:
- INFRA-2213: implement sampler-based trigger and expose parameters via feature flag (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- PR review: infra/pull/789 implements sigmoid function and decay; needs perf tests against nightly harness (owner: Alyssa Chen)
- Ops runbook: update scale-runbook with override criteria and regional min recommendations (owner: Jordan Blake)
- Telemetry: reduce metric scrape variance or apply sample-offset compensation in controller (owner: SRE team)

Appendix (notes, raw traces, quick logs):
- Example trace: 2024-11-08 13:02:12 us-west1 microburst 18s amplitude 2.7x -> deterministic triggered 2 scaleups in 45s, prob-majority triggered 0 scaleups, prob-sigmoid triggered 1 scaleup at 28s
- Cold-starts per scale event: deterministic 0.42, prob-majority 0.31, prob-sigmoid 0.27
- Cost modeling assumptions: A100-sim cost model, per-GPU-hour baseline rate, ignored spot preemption premiums for this run (follow-up needed)

Notes to reviewers:
- Data and all raw runs are in the attached folder on Drive (see linked_artifacts).
- If we proceed, plan a canary rollout to 20% of capacity for 2w with continuous p95 monitoring and auto-revert if p95 regresses >8% for >30m.
- Open question: whether to expose sampling window size to customers or gate behind workload profiles; proposing to keep sane defaults and expose advanced knobs via enterprise config only.

Unresolved questions / discussion points:
- What target for regional min GPUs is acceptable vs cost impact? (ap-chosen 3 in recommendation is conservative)
- How to model spot preemption interactions with probabilistic downscale? (next experiment)

Raw todo list:
- [ ] Add spot preemption to nightly simulation traces (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Instrument telemetry offset compensation in controller (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Draft rollout plan and customer communication (owner: Jordan)

End of sheet.
